A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeGLIF research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix E report original node-classification experiments on Cora, Citeseer, Amazon Photo, and binary variants, alongside denoising and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark, robustness, influence-validation, hybrid-model, and runtime results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The influence calculation, two noisy-node detectors, and relabelling rule remain unchanged. Section 5.4 adds a concrete hybrid variant that replaces the second-stage GCN with TSS, extending the training pipeline within the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds OGBN-Arxiv, PubMed, and the heterophilic Roman-Empire dataset, substantially extending graph size and structural coverage. Appendix E.2 also adds class-imbalanced and overlapping-class Cora scenarios. The original datasets and binary variants remain.

E2.justification: TSS joins the retained main benchmark comparator set in v2 Table 2 and receives additional comparisons under its preferred split. DirGNNConv is newly evaluated as the standalone comparator for Roman-Empire in Table 16. The original main-table comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The original main benchmark settings remain, but v2 introduces separate full-split TSS comparisons, group-removal experiments using 100 subsets per group size, and runtime/memory evaluations. New benchmark protocols include 400 clean nodes and hidden dimension 64 for OGBN-Arxiv, and a 50/25/25 split with DirGNNConv for Roman-Empire. Macro-F1 evaluation is also added.

E4.justification: v2 adds empirical checks of influence additivity and behavior without strict convergence, class-imbalance and overlap stress tests, split-sensitivity comparisons, and the TSS hybrid analysis. These examine previously untested assumptions and failure conditions. Existing clean-set-size, repeated-denoising, backbone, and threshold analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and standard deviations. v2 additionally introduces average-rank analysis and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests comparing both DeGLIF variants against TSS and RTGNN in Section 5, substantially expanding statistical support for comparative claims. Appendix E.1 also introduces Pearson-correlation estimation for influence validation.

E6.justification: The original main-table and binary results are retained apart from equivalent rounding. v2 adds substantial results for TSS, hybrid training, influence validation, runtime, and new scenarios. For example, Table 14 reports 36.7±3.6 for DeGLIF versus 31.6±2.7 for GCN at 50% pairwise noise on OGBN-Arxiv; these are newly evaluated results.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–3 and their Appendix C proofs are essentially retained. v2 explicitly extends the stated applicability to stationary points with invertible Hessians, derives the relabelling-weight bound, and adds an i.i.d.-sampling rationale for expected-risk claims. Section 6 and Appendix D add complexity and inverse-Hessian-vector-product formulations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central novelty, two-variant denoising contribution, and independence from noise-model knowledge. The revised discussion adds an explicit claim of practical scalability to OGBN-Arxiv, including execution where several competing methods encounter memory limits.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of graph-dependent influence approximations, baseline behavior on sparse versus dense graphs, split sensitivity, overlapping classes, and computational scalability. It also positions DeGLIF as complementary preprocessing for noise-robust learners. The overlap-specific relabelling interpretation remains uncertain because Tables 8 and 10 report identical values for different scenarios.

D1.justification: v2 discloses torch.linalg.inv usage, dataset-dependent weight decay, and the sampling strategy underlying the original splits. It adds architectures, clean-node budgets, splits, and data modifications for new experiments, plus measured resource costs. Code access changes from an anonymous short link to an explicitly identified GitHub repository; the PDFs do not establish changes to repository contents.

R1.justification: The principal novelty positioning and most original related-work discussion remain. v2 adds TSS, new dataset/backbone references, and literature on Hessian-vector methods and influence-approximation limitations. It also emphasizes complementing existing noise-robust methods through hybrid training.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: related work moves from Appendix D into Section 7, computational complexity becomes a dedicated section with a new appendix discussion, and a notation guide and assumption remarks are added. Experimental interpretation and discussion are extensively revised, alongside document-wide terminology and citation-style edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, v1 Tables 2–3 are transposed and consolidated into v2 Table 2, and the two main threshold figures are merged. The original relabelling table becomes prose, retained appendix plots are resized or relocated, algorithms are reformatted, and numerous new experimental tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1 through empirical validation of the influence approximation, comparisons under alternative splits, and measured scalability on larger and heterophilic graphs. These additions materially strengthen assessment of reliability and applicability while preserving the original results. Identical entries in the new imbalance and overlap relabelling tables weaken that particular analysis, but the broader validation gains remain substantial.
